summary.name: Augment Code Cosmos
summary.one_liner: Cosmos is Augment Code's agent orchestration platform for building always-on software delivery pipelines ("software factories") in which AI agents handle code review, ticket-to-PR work, vulnerability fixes and incident triage while engineers approve key checkpoints.
use_cases: automated first-pass code review on pull requests
turning Jira or Linear tickets into pull requests
investigating incidents before on-call engineers join
running end-to-end tests on code changes
orchestrating coding agents across an engineering organization
summary.what_it_does: Cosmos is a platform for running software development agents at organizational scale. It ships with pre-built "Experts" for stages of the SDLC: a Work Dispatcher for triaging tickets, a PR Author that takes a task to merge, a Code Review Fleet (Pair Review, Deep Code Review, PR Risk Analysis) that posts inline findings, and a Tester that exercises changes and posts results. Users can build loops in natural language, use experts from a library, fork them, or create their own, each with its own environment, capabilities and memory. Triggers include GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Linear, Jira, schedules and webhooks, and runs can go to managed cloud sandboxes or customer-controlled machines. The page also describes a context engine for codebase understanding, shared memory across runs, and approval gates where work pauses for human review.
notable: Pre-built 'Experts' for triage, authoring, code review and testing that can be forked or customized
Human approval gates built in: work pauses for review and consequential actions need a person's sign-off
Runs on managed cloud sandboxes, your own machines, or your own AWS/GCP infrastructure
Shared memory across runs, agents and teams so corrections carry over
caveats: The page gives no pricing details; the directory listing marks the tool as paid
Enterprise-oriented platform; the page does not describe a free tier or individual plan
Page is largely marketing copy, so specific capability claims are not independently verified
